# Mermaid Diagramming

Unknown words break a diagram and parameters fail silently, so validate in the host that will render it.

## Workflow

1. **Ground** - state every assumption; never invent an edge the supplied code, schema, or facts do not show. An architecture, schema, or refactor question is not by itself a request for a diagram. If the supplied material does not settle the type or a cardinality, state the assumption in the reply; when two types are equally plausible, ask one question. Before drawing, ask yourself: what question does this diagram answer (pick the type for it from authoring-rules.md section 1 "Choose the diagram type"), and would a reader get the answer in under 10 seconds? If not, cut detail or split.
2. **Fork.** [authoring-rules.md](references/authoring-rules.md) is mandatory on every path, in the sections below (cited by number and heading; both are fixed, so these citations stay valid):

   | Job | Read | Change |
   |---|---|---|
   | Parse repair: it fails to render | section 7 "Labels that break the parser"; the type file only if the error is not covered | syntax only; keep every node, edge, label, and meaning |
   | Semantic repair: it renders, but arrows, elements, cardinalities, or layout are wrong | section 7; for a flowchart also section 4 "Subgraphs for grouping"; the type file, including its traps | whatever restores the meaning the user intended; say what changed and why |
   | Appearance only: colors, theme, or config of a diagram that is otherwise right | section 6 "Contrast and classDef palette"; [advanced-features.md](references/advanced-features.md) when the theme or frontmatter config changes | styling only; keep every node, edge, and label; check text/fill contrast before validating |
   | New diagram, type obvious and unstyled | sections 1 "Choose the diagram type" and 7; the type file | everything |
   | New diagram, otherwise | sections 1-3 ("Choose the diagram type", "Direction and proportion", "Type-native controls") and 6-7 ("Contrast and classDef palette", "Labels that break the parser"); for a flowchart also 4-5 ("Subgraphs for grouping", "Shapes mean roles"); the type file | everything |

   For a mixed job (for example a semantic repair that also asks for new colors), take the union of the Read cells and apply the broader Change cell. When the type is plausible but not obvious, use the last row.

   Do NOT load `c4-diagrams.md` for `architecture-beta` or for repairing a non-C4 diagram. For a flowchart, authoring-rules.md sections 4-5 are the type reference.
3. **Draw, then self-check before validating.** Scan every flowchart node and edge label: is any `[ ] ( ) { } < > |` unquoted? (Sequence messages like `find(id)` are legal as written; do not quote them.) Is there a `#` or `;` in sequence text? Is lowercase `end` used as a node or participant id? Does a target whose name starts with `o` or `x` follow a link directly (`A---orders` parses as a circle edge to `rders`)? Intended circle or cross edges stay. Fix each from section 7; mmdc reports only the first parse error, and `#` fails silently.
4. **Validate** - `npx -y @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli -i in.mmd -o out.svg`. The CLI's bundled Mermaid decides what parses. Pinning the CLI does not pin Mermaid (an 11.x CLI depends on `mermaid ^11` and a 12.x CLI on `^12`, so an unpinned `npx` now resolves Mermaid 12 with its new defaults, see Renderer and host constraints; source https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli, checked 2026-11-13). Only when the user names the host's Mermaid version, validate in a scratch project whose package manager overrides `mermaid` to that exact version, and report the version actually installed; for GitHub or an unknown host, validate unpinned and name in the reply any version-gated construct from "Renderer and host constraints" that the diagram uses. Rerun after each fix; after three failing rounds, stop and report the remaining parser error with your best version; the Gotchas check and the size check below apply only to a render that exits 0 and are not run after a failed third round. Once a render exits 0, check the source against the Gotchas below, which exit 0 does not catch, and the rendered SVG's size against section 2 "Direction and proportion"; for a new diagram, split it only when the rendered text is unreadable at about 900px or the diagram is taller than about three screens (a short, wide diagram whose text stays readable is kept); for a repair, only report the readability problem, never restructure. A Chromium sandbox error (`No usable sandbox`, `--no-sandbox`) is not a diagram error, but the `--no-sandbox` retry runs Chromium with reduced isolation: use that config only for a trusted local diagram, tell the user the isolation is reduced, and ask before using it when the input comes from an untrusted source. To use it, create a uniquely named scratch file (`CFG=$(mktemp --suffix=.json)`), write `{"args":["--no-sandbox"]}` into it with `printf '%s' '{"args":["--no-sandbox"]}' > "$CFG"`, rerun with `-p "$CFG"` and delete it afterwards; never write the config into the working directory or the project (`-p` with a mktemp path ran with mmdc 12.2.0, checked 2026-11-14). If it still cannot run (no network, no Chromium), say in the reply that the diagram was not validated and list as unverified each construct you changed or added (for example the newly quoted labels, `<br/>` line breaks, a renamed `End` node, entity codes such as `#35;`), plus any version-gated syntax the diagram uses (for example `architecture-beta`).

| Type chosen | Read |
|---|---|
| Sequence | [sequence-diagrams.md](references/sequence-diagrams.md) |
| Class | [class-diagrams.md](references/class-diagrams.md) |
| ERD | [erd-diagrams.md](references/erd-diagrams.md) |
| C4 | [c4-diagrams.md](references/c4-diagrams.md) |
| architecture-beta | [architecture-diagrams.md](references/architecture-diagrams.md) |
| State, Git, Gantt, or Pie | [other-diagrams.md](references/other-diagrams.md) |
| Flowchart | authoring-rules.md sections 4-5 (the flowchart reference) |
| Frontmatter theme, look, layout (ELK), themeVariables, click, export flags and Docker, accessibility | [advanced-features.md](references/advanced-features.md) |

## Renderer and host constraints

- `architecture-beta` needs a Mermaid version that supports it; render once with the installed mmdc and check support in the target renderer before using it, and, when the host cannot render it, fall back to a flowchart. Older hosts print a syntax error or raw text. When the user asked for `architecture-beta` by name, never switch to a flowchart silently: first tell a syntax error in the diagram from an unsupported version, report which one it was, and ask before substituting a flowchart (the flowchart is the offered fallback when the host cannot render it). mmdc exits 0 for a failing `architecture-beta` and writes an SVG that reads "Syntax error in text", so grep the SVG, not the exit code. To tell the two apart, render a one-service diagram (`architecture-beta` plus `service db(database)[Database]`): if it renders cleanly, the error is in the user's diagram, so fix it; if it fails too, the renderer does not support the type (both checked with mmdc 12.2.0, 2026-11-14). Without a named request, the flowchart fallback stays. The `architecture-beta` icons are ONLY `cloud`, `database`, `disk`, `internet`, `server`. Never write `aws:`, `logos:`, or any other prefixed icon unless the user names a renderer that registers that pack. When the user asks for AWS, Docker, or other vendor logos, say in the reply that `aws:` and `logos:` icons render as `?` wherever the host did not register the pack (check GitHub and the VS Code preview), and that built-in icons are used instead.
- `architecture-beta` edge labels (`a:R -[HTTPS]-> L:b`) parse in Mermaid 11.17 and 12.3 (tested 2026-11-13) but not on every host; for GitHub put the protocol in the service title or use C4 `Rel`.
- Expanded node shapes `A@{ shape: cyl }` need a Mermaid version that supports them: render once with the installed mmdc and check support in the target renderer before using them, and fall back to the bracket shape (`A[("Text")]` for a cylinder) when it fails. Bracket shapes work everywhere.
- Frontmatter `config` needs a Mermaid version that supports it; older hosts ignore it or print it as text. `look: handDrawn` likewise needs a version that supports the look option. Render once with the installed mmdc and check support in the target renderer before using either; when the host's version is unknown, validate in that host (step 4). Since Mermaid 12.0.0 `layout: elk` is bundled and registered automatically; only a host older than 12, or the tiny build, needs `@mermaid-js/layout-elk` registered, otherwise it falls back to dagre (source for the elk sentence only: https://mermaid.js.org/config/layouts.html, which states "ELK is bundled and default from v12.0.0", the tiny build and its dagre fallback; checked 2026-11-14).
- Mermaid 12.0.0 changed the defaults: flowchart, state, class and ER diagrams re-lay out with `layout: elk` and recolour with theme `redux-color` and look `neo` (sequence diagrams change theme and look too). To keep or restore the Mermaid 11 appearance, put `theme: default`, `look: classic` and `layout: dagre` in the frontmatter config ([advanced-features.md](references/advanced-features.md), "Themes, look and layout"). `classDef` rules that set fill, stroke and color are unaffected; unclassed nodes follow the theme (sources https://mermaid.js.org/config/theming.html and the mermaid@12.0.0 notes at https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases, checked 2026-11-13).
- GitHub bundles its own Mermaid, which can differ from the CLI's: it lays out C4 its own way (labels may overlap or clip) and may lag on newer gitGraph options. Check the rendered result there, not only in Mermaid Live; a ```` ```mermaid ```` block containing only `info` prints the host's Mermaid version (source https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/creating-diagrams, checked 2026-11-13).

## Gotchas

These cost the most because the renderer accepts them, or because the cue to open the right file is easy to miss.

- NEVER write `Child <|-- Parent`: the arrowhead sits on the parent, and the inverted hierarchy renders with no error ([class-diagrams.md](references/class-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER reuse a C4 id: every Person, System, Container, and Component id must be unique across the diagram. A repeated id raises no error and silently redirects `Rel` arrows to the wrong element ([c4-diagrams.md](references/c4-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER write a gantt date in a format other than the declared `dateFormat`: it raises no error and the bar is drawn with a wrong span ([other-diagrams.md](references/other-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER read an ER cardinality glyph from the wrong end: each glyph describes the entity it touches, so `CUSTOMER }o--|| ORDER` (many customers per order) renders as happily as the intended `CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER` ([erd-diagrams.md](references/erd-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER put a `classDef` class on `[*]`: it is a parse error; style the first real state instead ([other-diagrams.md](references/other-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER leave out or mark optional the reply to a request in a detailed synchronous request/response sequence (anything the user describes call by call, or where they mention an answer coming back): draw a `-->>` reply for a `->>` call when the supplied facts establish that a reply exists (the user says an answer comes back, or the code returns a value); when the source specifies a call but not its reply, add the reply only as a labelled assumption (a note, or "(assumed)" in the label) or ask, and when the user says a call is fire-and-forget use `-)`. A high-level overview may omit replies on purpose; say so. A syntax-only repair never adds reply edges. Two silent sequence traps live in [sequence-diagrams.md](references/sequence-diagrams.md): a label used where the alias id belongs creates a second participant, and an unbalanced `+`/`-` activation runs to the bottom.
- NEVER give a pie slice a negative value: it is a parse error ([other-diagrams.md](references/other-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER `checkout` a gitGraph branch before its `branch` line; it is a parse error. Add the `branch` line at the commit the branch really started from ([other-diagrams.md](references/other-diagrams.md)).
- NEVER link a node inside a flowchart subgraph to a node outside it while relying on that subgraph's `direction`: Mermaid silently drops the `direction` ([authoring-rules.md](references/authoring-rules.md) section 4 "Subgraphs for grouping").
- NEVER leave a raw `#` in sequence message text: the rest of the message silently disappears (section 7 "Labels that break the parser").
- The most frequent parse failures are lowercase `end` as an id (it closes a block), an unquoted `(` in a label (it opens a second shape), and a target starting with `o` or `x` right after a link (`A---orders` becomes a circle edge to `rders`); step 3 scans for them, and the fixes are in section 7.
